        Root cause:
        The bug was caused by the function `gpiolib_dev_init()` returning `0` (indicating success) when the registration of the GPIO stub driver failed, instead of returning a negative error code. This could lead to incorrect assumptions about the success of the initialization process, potentially causing further issues in the system that relies on the GPIO library being properly initialized.
        
        Commit message:
        gpiolib: Fix error return code in gpiolib_dev_init()

Fix to return a negative error code from the error handling
case instead of 0, as done elsewhere in this function.

Fixes: 4731210c09f5 ("gpiolib: Bind gpio_device to a driver to enable fw_devlink=on by default")
Reported-by: Hulk Robot <hulkci@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: Wei Yongjun <weiyongjun1@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: Bartosz Golaszewski <bgolaszewski@baylibre.com>  
        
        Patch:
        diff --git a/drivers/gpio/gpiolib.c b/drivers/gpio/gpiolib.c
index 7ec0822c0505..6635e4ec60ce 100644
--- a/drivers/gpio/gpiolib.c
+++ b/drivers/gpio/gpiolib.c
@@ -4256,7 +4256,8 @@ static int __init gpiolib_dev_init(void)
 		return ret;
 	}
 
-	if (driver_register(&gpio_stub_drv) < 0) {
+	ret = driver_register(&gpio_stub_drv);
+	if (ret < 0) {
 		pr_err("gpiolib: could not register GPIO stub driver\n");
 		bus_unregister(&gpio_bus_type);
 		return ret;
--
